title: Culturing Mouse Cardiac Valves in the Miniature Tissue Culture System
protocol: Disinfect forceps and micro scissors with 70% ethanol.
Prepare a 5 ml syringe with 21G needle using sterile Tyrode’s Buffer.
Prepare a 5 ml syringe with 21G needle using sterile KCl solution (100 mM).
Prepare 65 ml of medium per heart: DMEM supplemented with 10% Fetal Calf Serum, antibiotic/antimycotic (A/A), and Insulin-Transferrin-Selenium (ITS).
Sterilize the perfusion chamber by spraying with 70% ethanol.
Dry the perfusion chamber with a paper towel.
Sterilize the bubble trap by spraying with 70% ethanol.
Dry the bubble trap with a paper towel.
Assemble the MTCS without initially attaching the perfusion chamber.
Position the bubble trap on the stand.
Using silicon tubing, make connections between the reservoir and the pump.
Connect the pump to the bubble trap using silicon tubing.
Make connections between the bubble trap and the reservoir with silicon tubing.
Ensure tubing inside the incubator is long enough for medium circulation and gas equilibrium.
Fill the 50 ml tube with 70% ethanol.
Turn on the pump at a flow speed of around 1 ml/min.
Circulate ethanol through the system for 30 min to sterilize all tubing.
Empty the reservoir and pump out ethanol from the system.
Fill the 50 ml tube with sterile distilled water.
Turn on the pump and circulate water through the system for 30 min.
Empty the reservoir and pump out water from the system.
Fill the 50 ml tube with 45 ml of medium.
Put the stand in the incubator.
Turn on the pump at a flow speed of around 1 ml/min to fill tubing with medium.
Circulate medium through the system for at least 1 hour to remove air bubbles and adapt to gas composition.
Maintain the incubator at standard tissue-culture conditions (5% CO2 and 37 °C).
Inject the mouse with 500 units of Heparin.
Wait for 10 minutes.
Anesthetize the mouse in an induction chamber with 4% isoflurane using a precision vaporizer.
Maintain anesthesia by connecting a facemask to a coaxial circuit.
Disinfect the fur of the mouse with 70% alcohol.
Open the abdominal cavity to expose the vena cava and diaphragm.
Make lateral incisions from the last rib to the first rib, reflecting the thoracic cage over the mouse’s head.
Insert a 21G needle attached to a 5 ml syringe containing sterile Tyrode’s Buffer into the inferior vena cava from the abdominal cavity through the diaphragm.
Perfuse Tyrode’s Buffer gently and with constant pressure into the vena cava until the heart loses some of its red color.
Replace the needle with a 21G needle attached to a 5 ml syringe containing sterile KCl solution.
Gently perfuse the KCl solution into the vena cava until the heart stops beating and remove the needle.
Lift the heart using curved forceps.
Dissect the heart free from surrounding tissue but leave arteries and veins proximal to the heart intact and attached to the heart.
Transfer the heart to a 15 ml tube containing ice-cold PBS supplemented with antibiotic/antimycotic (A/A).
Store the heart in ice-cold PBS for up to 3 hours.
Transfer the isolated heart from the 15 ml tube to a 10 cm Petri dish and add PBS supplemented with A/A.

Under a dissecting microscope, use scissors and forceps to remove all non-cardiac tissue but preserve the ascending aorta to at least the bifurcation with the brachiocephalic artery and the pulmonary veins, 2 mm proximal to the heart.
Cut off the tip of the apex of the heart to create access to the left ventricular lumen (typically 2 mm).
Place the perfusion chamber in the laminar flow hood under the dissecting microscope.
Attach a 5 ml syringe with medium to the insert needle using the silicone tubing.
Fill the perfusion chamber with 20 ml of medium.
Place the heart on the rotation stage between the two blunted needles in the perfusion chamber.
Adjust the height of the rotation stage so that the heart is positioned in front of the needles.
Ligate the aorta with suture (silk 7.0).
Ligate the left atrial appendage with suture.
Insert needle number 1 through the pulmonary vein into the left atrium and ligate proximal to its entry point.
Ensure that needle number 1 is not too far into the left atrium to avoid damaging the mitral valve.
Insert needle number 2 with a linear motion into the left ventricle.
Transfer medium from the perfusion chamber to a 50 ml tube.
Seal the needle to the myocardium with biocompatible glue.
After the glue has dried, carefully inject medium into the heart by connecting a medium-filled syringe to needle number 1.
Check for any leakage around needle number 1.
Ensure that medium exits from needle number 2 and perfuses out the last remaining blood from the heart.
Insert the needle in the aorta and ligate with suture.
Ensure the needle is not too far into the aorta to avoid damaging the aortic valve.
Insert the second needle with linear motion into the left ventricle.
Transfer medium from the perfusion chamber to a 50 ml tube.
Seal the second needle to the myocardium with biocompatible glue.
Wait for the glue to dry completely.
Inject medium into the heart using a syringe connected to the second needle.
Check for any leakage by observing if medium exits from the first needle and blood is perfused out of the heart.
Fill up the perfusion chamber with 20 ml of transferred medium.
Place gasket and lid on the chamber and tighten with washer and screws.
Attach the perfusion chamber to the stand.
Connect tubing as specified (see Figure 1D).
Place the stand in the incubator set at 5% CO2 and 37°C.
Connect the tubing to the pump.
Turn on the pump with a flow speed of around 600 μl/min.
Ensure the medium level allows visualization of flow by observing falling medium drops.
